title: Admissible coefficient stages and actual scalar functors for mixed cups
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum $D$ of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber] and its distinct coefficient prime $\ell$ and fixed algebraic closure $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ as in [sk-def-set]. For each finite subextension $F\subset\Omega$ use the actual field, valuation ring and quotient rings of [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. The coefficient stages are the tagged rings $A_{F,n+1}$ for $n\in\mathbf N$, $\mathcal O_F$, $F$ and $\Omega$. On the small pro-etale site of a scheme $W$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], associate their existing ambient categories, integral derived-complete constructible category, raw rationalized category [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] and common finite-stage category [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. Restrict each to the finite-Tor constructible domain of [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], which at the two field stages is the full category. Use the existing operations and tensor of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] and [def-pod-mixed-support-cup-product].

An admissible coefficient passage is a finite composable expression generated by: any unital ring homomorphism $A_{F,n+1}\to A_{G,m+1}$; integral reduction $\mathcal O_F\to A_{F,n+1}$; the inclusions $\mathcal O_F\to\mathcal O_G$ and $F\to G$ for $F\subset G$; localization $\mathcal O_F\to F$; inclusion $F\to\Omega$; and identities. Its coefficient homomorphism is the corresponding actual homomorphism, composed for successive passages. Its site functor is derived scalar extension at finite levels [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], the actual derived integral reduction [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction], the completed integral extension [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension], rational scalar extension, raw localization, or common-stage inclusion, respectively; a composite expression acts by composition. Its coefficient-complex functor is the normalized ordinary-module derived scalar extension along its coefficient homomorphism, in the common lifted coefficient universe. The reduction coefficient map uses the quotient identification of [lem-pod-point-sections-derived-reduction-data]. There is no field-to-finite-ring reduction generator.
